messages:
incident_bot: PAGE: High error rate detected for opal-corp (VPC) canary - 5xx spike on dedicated pool *opal-dedicated-2* — https://status.redwood.example/incident/1865432100
chris_oncall: On it. digging into metrics now.
maria_sre: I see request-failure% jumped from 0.3% to 12% at 15:07 UTC. latency OK but errors are all 502/504 from runtime.
kate_csm: Customer (Opal) just DM'd support, reporting failed requests from their integration. They've paused traffic on their side but want an ETA.
alex_platform: Canary is at 10% traffic, pinned artifact on canary is `rwd-artifact:v2026-03-15-98af3b` (new runtime kernel). Stable pool is `rwd-artifact:v2026-02-28-f7e1c2`.
lia_sre: Quick ask: can we drop canary to 0 and redirect to stable while we investigate? Prefer safe surgical swap rather than full revert.
jordan_eng: Agree. If we reduce canary and pin stable we avoid cross-tenant restart. We should also isolate Opal tenant to not get impacted by canary traffic.
chris_oncall: Steps I propose:
1) pin stable artifact to Opal dedicated pool (no model change)
2) reduce canary traffic to 0% for Opal routing policy
3) monitor error rate for 5m
4) if steady, return traffic but keep canary disabled for Opal until root cause
chris_oncall: Running pin now — using tooling: 
```
# pin stable artifact for tenant opal-corp
redwoodctl tenants pin --tenant opal-corp --artifact rwd-artifact:v2026-02-28-f7e1c2 --pool opal-dedicated-2
```
chris_oncall: CLI returned: "pin request accepted, job 98274"
alex_platform: I'll reduce canary routing for tenant.
alex_platform: Running: 
```
redwoodctl routing update --tenant opal-corp --canary-percent 0 --pool opal-dedicated-2
```
alex_platform: Routing update queued, push id 4431.
maria_sre: Metrics: error rate down to 1.1% (from 12%) within 90s of routing change. Good sign.
kate_csm: I told Opal we switched them back to stable; waiting for confirmation on their end. They say they see errors dropping.
lia_sre: Can we keep the canary artifact frozen and remove it from Opal's routing policies? Also create a temporary tenant rule to force-stable for next 24h.
jordan_eng: Creating dedicated rule now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rules create --tenant opal-corp --rule force_artifact --artifact rwd-artifact:v2026-02-28-f7e1c2 --duration 24h
```
jordan_eng: Rule created (rule-cc-710).
chris_oncall: Monitoring 5m sliding window — errors stable ~0.9%. No increase in latency.
maria_sre: Looking at runtime logs for the pinned canary artifact `v2026-03-15-98af3b`: multiple segfaults in fused-attention kernel under specific sequence lengths (>=2048). Reproducer attached to internal bug (BUG-4862).
alex_platform: Good catch. That explains canary-only failures. We should block rolling that artifact to other customers until fix/rollback.
kate_csm: Notifying Opal CSM & engineering contact: short update posted. They want postmortem and timeline.
lia_sre: Action items:
- chris_oncall: keep pin & force-rule in place until follow-up (done)
- jordan_eng: remove canary from Opal routing and label artifact quarantined (in progress)
- alex_platform: create capacity fallback if artifact propagates elsewhere
- maria_sre: file root-cause and repro steps to BUG-4862 and assign to runtime team
- kate_csm: customer comms + timeline
chris_oncall: Handoff to li a (overnight SRE). Lia, I left notes and job ids. If you need an immediate rollback to older artifact let me know, but stable looks good. :white_check_mark:
lia_sre: Thanks. I'll take over monitoring for next 3h and confirm with Opal. If errors reappear >2% escalate and we'll run full revert for the pool.
kate_csm: Opal acknowledges. Wants a short post-incident summary and an ETA on runtime patch.
jordan_eng: I'll tag the runtime engineers on BUG-4862, expected triage within 4 hours.
maria_sre: Logging done. Will attach log snippets and sequence-length histogram to the bug.
alex_platform: Quarantined artifact `v2026-03-15-98af3b` (label: quarantined, block-propagation: true).
lia_sre: Closing thread for now, monitoring. If anything changes I'll reopen. Thank you all. :thumbsup:
